summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update10.json → valid=true). Refinement of the previous turn's election-threshold finding, driven by its own weakest link: a stale lower threshold only matters if the candidate can collect the grants, and the vote rules gate collection on the voter's own view. Recorded as one Behavior plus a successor interpretation for the same question (previous opinion and counterevidence preserved, not replaced). The gate: requestVote refuses whenever the receiver knows a leader that is not the candidate and the request is not transfer-marked (raft.go:1650-1656), the mark being the one thing the voting side honours regardless of the leader it knows; and a voter's leader record is cleared exactly at the start of its own heartbeat-timeout handling, before it decides whether it is even eligible to campaign (raft.go:219-245). Consequences now stated precisely: for a candidacy without the transfer mark, a stale lower threshold can only be exploited where the canvassed voters have themselves lost their leader record — a degrading cluster, not a healthy one — so the earlier phrasing that a node 'may declare leadership with fewer grants than the majority it now holds' now carries that gate; for a timeoutNow-induced candidacy the gate is open by construction, so the previously recorded split-vote consequence stands with its configuration-growth condition; and in a healthy cluster where voters still know the leader, a stale threshold cannot be converted into a win. The underlying justification gap is unchanged — the count deciding the win is not the majority of the configuration the node holds when it takes office — and the mechanism, capture site and win test remain as recorded. Counterevidence kept explicit, including that an empty leader record is necessary but not sufficient for a grant (membership and log-freshness rules still apply) and that no execution was performed.
